title: Huevos Rancheros
subtitle: fried eggs on tomato salsa and warm tortillas
excerpt: A Mexican ranch breakfast built on a bold tomato and chilli salsa with eggs cooked directly in the sauce. Flour tortillas go underneath. It is ready in 20 minutes and feeds a hungry table without much effort.
sourceNotes: Huevos rancheros -- ranch eggs -- originated as a mid-morning meal for Mexican farmworkers. It became popular across Mexico and the American Southwest during the 20th century.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The salsa can be made up to 3 days ahead.

content.text: Make the salsa first and let it cook down while you warm the tortillas. The eggs cook in the salsa at the end, so everything is ready at the same time.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and red pepper for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, cumin, and chilli flakes. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the tinned tomatoes and season with salt. Simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce is thick.
Make four wells in the sauce. Crack an egg into each well. Cover the pan and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or directly over a gas flame for 30 seconds each side.
Serve each egg on a tortilla with a generous spoonful of salsa. Top with fresh coriander if you have it.

items.symptom: Egg whites are set but yolks are also solid
items.fix: Check after 3 minutes and remove from the heat as soon as the whites are set.
Simmer uncovered for another 5 minutes until it thickens.

content.text: Huevos rancheros began as morning fuel for farm labourers in Mexico. The name simply means ranch eggs. It spread north with Mexican communities and became popular across the American Southwest, where it is now a fixture of brunch menus. The dish varies by region -- black beans, avocado, or cheese are all common additions.
